title: 123. Divine Mercy - Day of the Great Judgment!

reels.title: Without judgment there is no mercy: Jesus is not only a merciful savior
reels.hook: This day is not written in any of your calendars
reels.why: It starts from a powerful image of God's calendar and our departure from the world, and leads to a paradox that surprises: only a judge can show mercy. The thought is well-rounded and has a clear point.
reels.speaker: Vladimir Grebenar
reels.quote: Without judgment there is no mercy.

cards.text: This day is not written in any of your calendars
Vladimir Grebenar · host, Ora et Labora
Saint Paul in the Epistle to the Philippians admonishes believers to prepare for the “day of Christ”.
“Without judgment there is no mercy.”
Divine Mercy – Day of the Great Judgment!

reels.title: How to know if you are doing God's will? Ask him like a child asks a father
reels.hook: Do you ask God in the morning: what should I do today?
reels.why: A simple family comparison that everyone immediately understands turns the abstract “will of God” into concrete daily advice.
reels.speaker: Vladimir Grebenar
reels.quote: But if you don't ask me, how will you carry it out?

cards.text: Do you ask God in the morning: what should I do today?
Vladimir Grebenar · host, Ora et Labora
From the interpretation of the psalm about the “assembly of the upright”, those who do the will of God.
“You can only if you ask me. But if you don't ask me, how will you carry it out?”
Divine Mercy – Day of the Great Judgment!

reels.title: Mocking charismatics? A warning about the sin against the Holy Spirit
reels.hook: Mocking miracles? This, it is said, is not forgiven
reels.why: A sharp, provocative message aimed directly at today's commenting on social networks. It has a clear stance, a concrete example, and a strong conclusion with Saint Paul.
reels.speaker: Vladimir Grebenar
reels.quote: If someone is praying and healing, signs and wonders are happening, keep silent and do not speak up.

cards.text: Mocking miracles? This, it is said, is not forgiven
Vladimir Grebenar · host, Ora et Labora
Jesus healed a man with dropsy on the Sabbath (Lk 14:1-6), and the Pharisees condemned it.
“If someone is praying and healing, signs and wonders are happening, keep silent and do not speak up.”
Saint Paul, full of charisms, “baptized half of Europe”
Divine Mercy – Day of the Great Judgment!

reels.title: Jesus knew they were setting a trap for him and went in anyway
reels.hook: He knew it was a trap. And yet he went in.
reels.why: The story has tension (trap), a twist (Jesus asks the question first), and a hard conclusion: after the testimony there is no longer the excuse “I didn't know”.
reels.speaker: Vladimir Grebenar
reels.quote: He goes directly into confrontation on the front line.

cards.text: He knew it was a trap. And yet he went in.
Vladimir Grebenar · host, Ora et Labora
The Pharisees invited Jesus to a meal on the Sabbath to catch him in a wrong word (Lk 14:1-6).
“You cannot say: I didn't know.”
Divine Mercy – Day of the Great Judgment!

reels.title: Raised hands and singing are not enough: “Depart from me, you evildoers”
reels.hook: Do you sing to God, but he does not recognize you?
reels.why: A provocative contrast between external praise and the actual doing of God's will, supported by Jesus' words that the viewer recognizes.
reels.speaker: Vladimir Grebenar
reels.quote: Not a community of people who merely raise their hand in the air and sing to God.

cards.text: Do you sing to God, but he does not recognize you?
Vladimir Grebenar · host, Ora et Labora
The host interprets the psalm: “I will praise the Lord with all my heart in the assembly of the upright.”
“Depart from me, you evildoers.”
Divine Mercy – Day of the Great Judgment!

reels.title: The Pharisees did not have a bad example before them. We have it.
reels.hook: They did not have a warning. We have it.
reels.why: A brief, well-rounded insight with an unexpected turn: the Pharisees were first, and today we have their example and repeat it again. It ends with a clear image of “turning to the other side”.
reels.speaker: Vladimir Grebenar
reels.quote: You see a miracle, you see the living Jesus, you see that something is happening and the Pharisee, if you listen to him, turns you to the other side.

cards.text: They did not have a warning. We have it.
Vladimir Grebenar · host, Ora et Labora
In the Gospel, Jesus warns against the “leaven of the Pharisees”.
“You see a miracle, you see the living Jesus… the Pharisee, if you listen to him, turns you to the other side.”
Divine Mercy – Day of the Great Judgment!

reels.title: They invited Jesus to a meal only to catch him
reels.hook: They invited him to lunch, but to catch him
reels.why: A clear image of deceitfulness and an unexpected response: Jesus goes anyway because he cares deeply about the conversion of those setting a trap for him.
reels.speaker: Vladimir Grebenar
reels.quote: Jesus cares deeply about their conversion.

cards.text: They invited him to lunch, but to catch him
Vladimir Grebenar · host, Ora et Labora
Lk 14:1-6: Jesus dines on the Sabbath in the house of a Pharisee leader.
“Jesus cares deeply about their conversion.”
Divine Mercy – Day of the Great Judgment!
